1. The present appeal is filed by the appellant-insurance company under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment dated 22/08/2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi.),
Panchmahals at Godhara in MACP No.848 of 2009.

sentences.text:
2. Short facts of the claim case are as under:
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/284/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined 2.1.

On 18/05/2009, deceased Gulabbhai @ Ranjitsinh Fulabhai Patel was driver in truck of opponent no.4 bearing registration no.GJ-17-T-9959 and he was driving the truck in slow and careful manner on the left side of the road.

When he was passing the place of the accident at about 10:30 hours, at that time, opponent no.1 came in truck bearing registration no.GJ-09-Y-7279 in rash and negligent manner and with excessive speed and lost control and came on wrong side of the road and dashed with the truck of Gulabbhai and caused an accident.

Gulabbhai sustained serious injuries in the accident and immediately taken to the Civil Hospital,
Kheda but as the injuries were very serious in nature, he succumbed to the same.

2.2. The heirs and legal representatives of the deceased Gulabbhai therefore filed claim petition under the provisions of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.7,60,000/- against the respondents.

2.3. Vide the aforesaid impugned judgment, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the appellants- original claimants under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 holding the appellants-original claimants are entitled to an amount of Rs.6,58,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petition till its actual realization with proportionate costs and respondent nos.1 to 3 of the claim petition are directed to pay the amount of compensation jointly and severally.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/284/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined 2.4.
Aggrieved by the impugned judgment of the Tribunal, the Oriental Insurance Company who is respondent no.3 in the claim petition, filed the present appeal.

3. This Court vide order dated 03/04/2014, noticing the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellant- insurance company and the grounds raised in the present appeal, has admitted the appeal.

4. The learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in passing the impugned judgment and has failed to appreciate the evidence on record in its true perspective.
He has submitted that the appellant is wrongly held 100% negligent.
He has submitted that the learned Tribunal has failed to appreciate the FIR and Panchnama which reveal that the accident has occurred between the cross road.
The accident is not head on collusion.

The FIR and Panchnama also indicate that the deceased dashed his truck to the left side cabin of the truck insured with the appellant and therefore, the learned Tribunal ought to have considered 50%
contributory negligence of the deceased.
He has further submitted that the amount of compensation granted by the learned Tribunal is very high.

sentences.text:
The learned advocate for the appellant has therefore submitted that the impugned judgment of the Tribunal is not just, fair, and reasonable and the same is required to be interfered by this Court.
5.

Per contra, learned advocate for respondent no.6 for the United India Insurance Company Limited submitted at length facts of the impugned judgment on point of negligence and vehemently argued that the learned Tribunal, after appreciating all the facts of panchnama decided the negligence on part of the driver of the vehicle insured with the appellant-insurance company.
He has further submitted that the accident is not head on collision and referred the facts of panchnama of place of accident.
It is further submitted that the accident occurred on a cross road.

He has further submitted that the driver of the appellant-insurance company has not stepped into the witness box and the learned Tribunal has rightly held 100% negligence of the driver of the appellant insurance company and lastly prayed to dismiss the appeal.
6.

Learned advocate of the original claimants submitted at length facts of the subject matter and vehemently argued that the learned Tribunal accorded the detailed findings on point of negligence and the same is not required to be interfered and lastly prayed to dismiss the appeal.
7.

Heard learned advocates appearing for the respective NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/284/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined parties, on the disputes between the parties in narrow compass and perused the record and proceedings and impugned judgment, more particularly, the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while passing the impugned judgment.
8.
This Court has also considered the facts and circumstances of the subject matter and rival contentions of the learned advocates appearing for the concerned parties.

9. As regards the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellant on the issue of negligence, considering the facts and circumstances of the subject matter, learned advocate for the appellant referred the panchnama of place of accident vide Exh.26 and vehemently argued that the accident occurred on the cross road.
It is further submitted that the drivers of both the vehicles are required to take reasonable care.
It is further submitted that at the time of the accident, the deceased was also driving the truck.
It is further submitted that both the vehicles involved in the accident are heavy vehicles.
It is further submitted that both the drivers are negligent in the accident and vehemently argued on the point of contributory negligence.

It is further submitted that in the impugned judgment, 100% liability of the opposite truck driver is held which is not just, proper and reasonable and the learned Tribunal has failed to appreciate the facts of the panchnama and lastly argued that assessed 50%-50% negligence of both the vehicles involved in the accident should be considered.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/284/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined 9.1.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the subject matter, it appears that the original claimants Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Fulabhai Akhambhai Patel on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180058050/
3 are heirs and legal representatives of the the deceased driver of the truck bearing registration no.GJ-17-T-9959.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In other words, in the accident, the driver of the truck bearing registration no.GJ-17- T-9959 is succumbed to the accident.
9.2. Considering the facts of the FIR and panchnama of place of accident, it appears that the driver of the truck bearing registration no.GJ-09-Y-7279 filed the complaint of the said accident.
It appears from the record that the complainant is not stepped into the witness box.
But considering the facts of panchnama of place of accident, it appears that both the vehicles are damaged.
Cabin of the truck bearing registration no.GJ-17-T-9959 dashed with the truck bearing registration no.GJ-09-Y-7279.

This fact is required to be considered for determining the point of negligence.
9.3.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the subject matter and available material on record,
it appears that the deceased driver of the truck bearing registration no.GJ-17-T- 9959 is also negligent to some extent in occurrence of the accident.
Hence, contributory negligence is required to be considered for the truck bearing registration no.GJ-17-T-9959 to the extent of 20%.
In other words, driver of the truck bearing registration no.GJ-09-Y-7279 is required to be held negligent to the extent of 80%.
The same would be just, proper and reasonable.

Under the circumstances,
impugned NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/284/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined judgment is required to be interfered on the point of negligence as discussed above.
10.

Considering the record and proceedings available on record, copy of the insurance policy produced by respondent no.6 vide Exh.24, it appears from the said policy that the respondent insurance company has received premium of Rs.50/- for Workman Compensation (WC) employee.
In other words, respondent no.6 insurance company is liable to pay 20% awarded amount to the original claimants accordingly.

11. On the issue of quantum of compensation, learned advocate of the appellant submitted at length facts on the point of quantum decided in the impugned judgment and vehemently argued that the learned Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased on higher side which is not just and reasonable.
He has further submitted that the deceased was a truck driver and not produced any income proof of the deceased and therefore, notional income should be assessed.
11.1. Considering the contention of the learned advocate for the appellant on the issue of quantum of compensation, it appears from the record that the deceased was a truck driver.

Though the income proof of the deceased is not produced on record, in the impugned judgment, the income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.4,000/- per month considering the nature of work of the deceased at the time of accident.
The learned Tribunal has rightly recorded finding that the quantum of compensation must be liberal and not generous.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/284/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined

Keeping this principle in mind and considering the family status of the deceased, the income of the deceased assessed by the learned Tribunal at Rs.4,000/- per month appears to be just and reasonable and not required to be interfered at all.
Therefore, submissions of learned advocate of the appellant on this issue are not sustained.

In the appeal memo, the appellant has stated and referred the decision of this Court rendered in First Appeal No.2345 of 2005 and another in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs.
Jaysukhlal Maganlal Doshi and others reported in 2013 (3) GLR 2283.
12.1.

entities.text:
New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs.
Jaysukhlal Maganlal Doshi and others reported in 2013 (3) GLR 2283
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
I have gone through the same, more particularly para-19 of the said decision, which reads as under:
"19.

We are of the opinion, having regard to the evidence on record, that the defense of insurance company that the vehicle was used as a taxi to carry passengers for hire and reward and the same was in breach of the conditions of the insurance policy,.....".
12.2. Considering the facts and circumstances of the subject matter, there is no contention raised by the appellant- insurance company about breach of the conditions of the insurance policy.

Hence,
above cited decision cannot be made applicable in the present case.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/284/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined 13.

In view of aforesaid, impugned judgment is modified to the extent that the driver of the truck bearing registration no.GJ-09-Y-7279 is liable negligent to the extent of 80% and driver of the truck bearing registration no.GJ-17-T-9959 is liable negligent to the extent of 20%.
14.
For the foregoing reasons, present appeal is partly allowed to the aforesaid extent.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable for payment of award amount granted by the learned Tribunal vide impugned judgment.
15. Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned tribunal forthwith, if received.
